title: Dreischarf 2016a: VBR force, trunk inclination and knee bending in stoop vs squat lifting and lateral lifting
condition: lifting a crate (4-10.8 kg) from the ground by stoop or squat technique, or laterally with one hand

quantity.name: VBR resultant force in lifting
quantity.definition: ABSOLUTE maxima of the resultant VBR force (N); RELATIVE squat/stoop ratio of maximal resultant force (%, median and range over sessions); RELATIVE lateral vs frontal difference; trunk inclination and knee-bending at the time of maximal force (deg)

source.authors: Dreischarf M, Rohlmann A, Graichen F, Bergmann G, Schmidt H
source.sample: 4 male patients with telemeterised VBR (3 x L1, 1 x L3); 17 sessions, 104 stoop/squat lifts, 26 lateral lifts

patients.implant_note: VBR replaces parts of the fractured vertebral body and the adjacent discs; posterior internal fixator remains in situ

protocol.summary: Bottle crate lifted from the ground 2-4 times per technique per session; weights per patient in Table 1 (mostly 10.8 kg; also 10, 7, 4.3, 4 kg).
how_to_simulate: Stoop: knees ~10 deg, trunk inclination ~52 deg at max force; squat: knees ~45 deg, trunk ~39 deg (medians in data)
Hand load: crate (10.8 kg typical) held in both hands in front just after lift-off; lateral lift: same crate in one hand beside the feet
Output: segment compression at the VBR level; compare the squat/stoop ratio and lateral/front ratio
A whole-spine MSK model outputs total segment compression at the implant level, not the implant share; compare trends/relative changes unless the model includes the VBR and posterior fixator

subject_model.implant_note: VBR replaces parts of the fractured vertebral body and the adjacent discs; posterior internal fixator remains in situ

protocol.notes: Load measured on a telemeterised vertebral body replacement (modified Synex, 6 load components, accuracy ~2% force / 5% moment of 3000 N / 20 Nm calibration range) that shares the load with the posterior internal fixator, residual vertebral bone and bone graft; the VBR force is NOT the total spinal load. Maximal forces occurred shortly after crate lift-off, not at maximal inclination.

data.x: absolute maximum resultant force over all sessions, WP1
squat vs stoop, average difference in resultant force
frontal vs lateral one-hand lifting, average difference (lateral lower)
data.note: range printed as '1 to 25%' with the sign lost; 'in only one session ... differences of 1%'; 8 of 9 sessions higher in front

data.x: trunk inclination at max force, stoop
trunk inclination at max force, squat
knee bending at max force, stoop
knee bending at max force, squat
maximal trunk inclination during stoop lift
maximal knee bending during squat lift

extraction.from: Dreischarf 2016a abstract and Results 3.1-3.2 text (Figs 2-3 per-patient bars not digitised)
extraction.check_notes: Re-read Results; all values match. 'average of alpha_max = 63 deg' printed as average (stored as mean).

pass_rule.rule: relative change: model sign correct and |model - measured| <= half the inter-patient range (or 25 percentage points where no range is given)
